experiment.name: kimi_k3_kda_second_pass_exploration
experiment.hypothesis: fused streaming and persistent KDA state reduce memory and launch cost, but state locality only helps when local bandwidth and capacity justify it
experiment.stock_control: generic GPU control from the first sweep; it is not a B300 or Vera Rubin execution
experiment.scope: one KDA decode head; head dimensions 64/128/256; state-update density 1/2/4/8; INT4/INT8-like weights; 8/16-bit activations
experiment.quality_gate: all rows use the same deterministic workload-count model and only FPGA rows within KV260 proxy limits enter rankings
experiment.transfer_limit: does not establish model quality, full-layer performance, FPGA timing closure, ASIC frequency, or product GPU comparison

opportunities.observation: state locality reduces external bytes but adds local traffic and SRAM capacity pressure
competing_explanations: state update density is too low
state does not fit in the selected SRAM
opportunities.mechanism: keep the recurrent KDA state on chip across tokens
opportunities.falsifier: RTL or KV260 design shows state-local mode slower at matched clock and bandwidth
opportunities.next_measurement: state-local versus streamed-state RTL at head dimensions 128 and 256

opportunities.observation: fusion removes intermediate writes and permits overlap
competing_explanations: the assumed memory efficiency is optimistic
the intermediate tensor is already cached
opportunities.mechanism: wire projection, gate, state, and output stages as a streaming pipeline
opportunities.falsifier: RTL timing or buffering hazards erase the predicted latency reduction
opportunities.next_measurement: cycle-accurate pipeline simulation with backpressure and state feedback

opportunities.observation: more MACs help only until memory or resource limits dominate
competing_explanations: FPGA DSP packing changes the resource curve
opportunities.mechanism: size the reusable GEMV engine for the dominant projection work
opportunities.falsifier: larger arrays reduce measured frequency or leave DSPs idle
opportunities.next_measurement: sweep 64/128/256/512 MAC RTL blocks with real memory schedules
